notes: The page continues a construction of a canonical lifting along a quarter of a great circle, identifies a lift on two generators, and discusses partial sections on stabilizer subgroups. It introduces 0\prime=2, 1\prime=-1, and infinity\prime=1/2 and describes the three connected arcs of U^tau. The second stability subgroup is literally written Gamma_2, although the preceding fixed point is 1/2; it is preserved, not corrected. H explicitly supplied 1/2 from the mathematical context. That contextual discrepancy prompted inspection of the complete stability line. No mathematical proof check or outside reference was used here. The text begins and ends mid-argument. No independently written correction or mathematical question is added by the author on this sheet. The lower-left manuscript number is 27. Root rejected a semicolon after the first paragraph’s 0: the upper round mark is the numeral, not a punctuation dot. Independent second-reading crop B10 showed two canceled zones after tilde U, rather than one doubtful subscript. Both are now preserved with shape-based alternatives; their exact letters and attachment remain uncertain. B12 confirmed a distinct dot and tau stem, resolving the local added doubt without inferring an earlier canceled t. These are reading decisions, not mathematical checks.

adjudications.evidence: The opening q has its bowl left of the descending stroke, followed by a raised apostrophe and the low on run; it does not have a separate final s as puis would require. The next word has the p stem and a long compressed eu join ending in a t-like turn. Choisir is clear. Canoniquement has the q descender and a continuous ending reaching a crossed t; no separate superscript contraction is established. The final connector has the low e-entry and n join used for en. Retain the first wording, without expanding a newly inferred short form.

The first entry is heavily retraced but its standing dark stroke is a tall 1 with a lower return, followed by a clear comma. Lighter curves around its foot do not establish a complete zero or a recoverable revision sequence. The infinity sign and parentheses agree.
Par and transport are readable. The final word has the lower oval and tall loop of d followed directly by one low e-run with a downturned exit; there is no independently separable extra s. Retain de.

The former admits a parenthesized barred-P or script-E outline; the lower has stacked curling strokes compatible with script E or xi. Neither is securely deciphered. The single doubtful subscript in the first reading failed to preserve the upper canceled zone. Both zones are now represented, with narrow shape-based doubts; the live (P) to the right remains clear. The subscript position records the lower placement, not a certain original attachment.

A distinct small dark dot stands above the second tau's retraced upper bar, and the bent stem with lower return remains a readable tau. The retracing does not obscure either identifying feature. Resolve the first-pass local doubt to dotted tau. The first arrow has a left bar, and the second has a right arrowhead; arrow-length macro choices do not change the reading.
The final article consists of the tall l entry and a single low e ending with a down-hook. No independent terminal s follows it. The two-stroke verbal equality sign and pour are unchanged; retain le.

A single horizontal cancellation obscures the middle letters. The initial rounded traces and final long descending loop remain compatible with conj.; the ending and any point are not separately secure. The proposed longer conjug cannot be established from additional readable letters. Keep the entire short candidate doubtful, including its punctuation.

The canceled initial sign has a mostly straight upright and a top arm, with another short crossing that may belong to the cancellation. Gamma remains preferred; an F-like extra arm remains possible, while the proposed tau is not more clearly supported. The equalities 2=0-prime, -1=1-prime and 1/2=infinity-prime, including commas, agree. Fraction-size macros do not alter the reading.

The two Gamma subscripts are 0-prime and 1-prime; each set has a dotted sigma with the matching subscript and an ordinary tau. Both closing commas are visible. The comparison differences only move commas across math delimiters and insert spacing commands.

Gamma carries infinity-prime, sigma has a separate upper dot and infinity subscript, tau has no separate upper dot, and a comma follows the closing brace. Only the comma's position relative to the math delimiter differs.

The first connector is overworked into two intersecting loops, so en remains preferred but ou cannot be excluded from its strokes. The second connector has the simpler low e/n outline. The sigma/tau pairs, their subscripts, commas and final point agree; keep the first local doubt.

Between arcs and grand the looped d continues into a low e-ending, without a distinct u cup. The canceled short form has a p descender and a separate taller t-like rise crossed by the cancellation, supporting pt. The three numerical entries, their later primes and the live qui contiennent agree. Retain de and the readable canceled pt.
